description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, idiom 33: the program printed NOTHING on stdout -- the import error is on stderr).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.

REPRODUCERS (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/posix1.pl .. posix7.pl):
  use POSIX; print floor(3.7), " ", ceil(3.2), "\n";        perl "3 4"      PCL dies: Undefined subroutine &main::floor
  use POSIX qw(strftime); print strftime("%Y-%m-%d", gmtime(0));   perl 1970-01-01   PCL dies at the use: "strftime" is not exported by the POSIX module
  use POSIX qw(INT_MAX DBL_MAX EXIT_FAILURE);               PCL dies: "EXIT_FAILURE" is not exported
  use POSIX qw(floor ceil fmod); (explicit list of names the stub has)      identical to perl
`use POSIX qw(strftime)` and bare `use POSIX;` are the two commonest spellings in scripts (every log line, every date column), so this is a first-hour alpha failure.

LAYER (9a): a module fact => `lib/POSIX.pm`, plain Perl wherever plain Perl can say it (strftime over localtime/gmtime + sprintf WITH perl's mktime normalisation -- #1613 has the probe; mktime via the same arithmetic core Time::Local uses; ctime/asctime/difftime; floor/ceil/fmod/round/trunc/lround/fmax/fmin/copysign; strtol/strtod WITH perl's two-value return `(num, unparsed_length)` -- the stub's strtol ignores the base and always answers 0 unparsed; toupper/tolower; the limits/float constants; EXIT_SUCCESS/EXIT_FAILURE; WIFEXITED/WEXITSTATUS/WIFSIGNALED/WTERMSIG/WIFSTOPPED/WSTOPSIG as arithmetic on the status word; the SIG* numbers from the runtime's own signal table, not literals).  What needs the OS (`_exit`, `setsid`, `isatty`, `dup2`, `getpid`/`getppid`/`getuid`..., `uname`, `ttyname`, `pause`, `nice`, `access`, `mkfifo`, `strerror`, `errno`, `setlocale` answering "C"/the environment's name, `tmpnam` NOT -- perl removed it) goes through ONE OR TWO runtime primitives reached by the blessed shim-dispatch seam (`builtin::`-style, DECIDED s377), never a module or function name in `Pl/` or `cl/` beyond that seam.

ORDER THE SURFACE BY MEASUREMENT, not by the man page: census `POSIX::NAME` and `use POSIX qw(...)` lists over perl's own lib/ + the CPAN board corpus (`cpan-tests/modules/`) + perl's t/ (one perl one-liner; keep the ranked table in the task).  Implement from the top until the tail is names nobody in the three populations calls.  `@EXPORT` = perl's own default list (`perl -MPOSIX -e 'print "@POSIX::EXPORT"'`, 587 names) RESTRICTED TO WHAT THE SHIM IMPLEMENTS; perl's `@EXPORT_OK` extras likewise; the %EXPORT_TAGS perl has (`:sys_wait_h :fcntl_h :errno_h :limits_h :float_h :math_h :signal_h :stdlib_h :time_h :unistd_h :locale_h` ...) built the same way.  An UNIMPLEMENTED name stays loud (Exporter's "not exported" at the use, or "Undefined subroutine" at the call) -- never a stub that answers a plausible value (rule 12).

THE DEFAULT-EXPORT RISK, to probe BEFORE shipping it (the stub's own comment: "mirroring that wholesale would shadow user subs"): (1) a user file that defines its own `sub floor`/`sub round`/`sub isatty` AFTER `use POSIX;` -- perl: the user's wins (with a "redefined" warning); PCL must agree in both source orders; (2) names that are also PERL BUILTINS are NOT in perl's @EXPORT (they are EXPORT_OK only: close nice open pipe read sleep times write printf sprintf ...) -- keep it that way, because an imported sub named like a builtin does not override it in PCL (#1870, the sibling member); (3) compile-time cost: `use POSIX;` is in a great many scripts, so measure `pcl -e 'use POSIX; print 1'` cold and warm before/after and FLAG anything over ~0.1 s warm; (4) the bareword-constant form `print INT_MAX > 0 ? ...` must parse as a TERM (`()`-prototype crosses the use since #365 -- probe it).

PORTABILITY (USER standing: not software for our laptop): the stub hardcodes LINUX values (O_CREAT 64, the errno numbers), and so do lib/Fcntl.pm and lib/Errno.pm.  This task does NOT fix those two, but must not ADD new hardcoded platform numbers: a new OS constant comes from the runtime (sb-posix / sb-unix constants through the seam).  FILE the Fcntl/Errno half separately with a macOS probe if one can be had, else with the list of constants that differ between Linux and Darwin.

BAR: `lib/` change => full sweep + the companion files that `use POSIX` (`grep -a -l`), the CPAN board dists that use it by ROWS, guard rows in a NEW Pl/t/posix-01.t with perl as the oracle (strftime over the common conversions %Y %m %d %H %M %S %j %a %b %e %F %T %s %z-free, one out-of-range field for the normalisation, mktime round trip, the W* macros on real `system` statuses, strtol with a base and a trailing junk string, bare `use POSIX;` + a user sub of the same name in both orders), `prove --timer` on the new file.


=== DONE (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) ===
`lib/POSIX.pm` is now plain Perl with perl's OWN default export list
restricted to what it implements.  Surface: the math family (floor ceil fmod
pow fabs log2 log10 trunc round lround fmax fmin fdim hypot cbrt copysign
signbit isnan isinf nearbyint remainder), the ctype family, strftime / mktime
/ asctime / ctime / difftime / clock / tzset / tzname, the :sys_wait_h macros
as arithmetic on the status word, strtod / strtol / strtoul WITH perl's
two-value return, the limits / float / errno / locale / fcntl constants,
errno / strerror / setlocale / localeconv, access / dup / isatty / _exit /
getpid / getppid / getcwd, and the SIG* numbers.

Two things no Perl can say go through the blessed `builtin::` seam: a signal
NAME's number (read from the runtime's own table -- no shim freezes this
machine's numbers into Perl source) and an immediate exit.  strftime
MKTIME-NORMALISES its fields as perl's does, over a days-from-civil
computation with NO Time::Local dependency, and DIES naming any conversion it
does not implement (rule 12).

THE PARSE FACT MATTERED MORE THAN THE FUNCTIONS: POSIX was in
`_extract_module_prototypes`'s skip list, so its constants' `()` prototypes
never crossed the `use`, and `print INT_MAX - 1, " ", EXIT_FAILURE + 1, "\n"`
read as `INT_MAX(-1, ...)` -- one call swallowing the rest of the argument
list.  POSIX and Time::HiRes both leave that list (Carp stays in it).

The four RISKS were probed before shipping and are guard rows: a user sub of
the same name in BOTH orders; builtin-named names staying out of @EXPORT (an
imported sub named like a builtin now DISPLACES it -- #1870 -- so a default
export of `abs` would silently change every `abs` in the file); the
bareword-constant term; and the warm cost -- `pcl -e 'use POSIX; print 1'` is
0.052 s against 0.039 s for a bare program (+13 ms, under the task's 0.1 s
gate; the 2.4 s a first measurement showed is ./runpcl's cache-off path, filed
#2055).

Guard Pl/t/posix-01.t, 16 rows with perl as the oracle, inverse-verified on a
5ce155cb extraction where 13 fail.  What is deliberately absent -- the OO
classes, the sig* family, sysconf/pathconf, setsid/mkfifo/pause/nice/
ttyname/dup2/chroot/uname, and setlocale's "it changes nothing" -- is in
docs/not-supported.md, loud at the use or at the call, never a stub.
No NEW hardcoded platform numbers: the signal numbers come from the runtime.


=== DONE (s492c) ===
SHIPPED s492c member 2 (cf95099d), closing #1613.  lib/POSIX.pm is plain Perl
with perl's own default export list RESTRICTED to what it implements: the math
and ctype families, strftime / mktime / asctime / ctime / difftime, the
:sys_wait_h macros, strtod / strtol / strtoul with perl's two-value return,
the limits / float / errno / locale / fcntl constants, errno / strerror,
access, dup, isatty, _exit.  Two things no Perl can say (a signal NAME's
number, an immediate exit) go through the `builtin::` seam, so no shim freezes
this machine's numbers into Perl source.  THE PARSE FACT MATTERED MORE: POSIX
left `_extract_module_prototypes`'s skip list, so its constants' `()`
prototypes cross the `use` and `print INT_MAX - 1, ...` stops reading as
INT_MAX(-1, ...).  Warm cost +13 ms.  Guard Pl/t/posix-01.t, 16 rows.
subject: EVERYDAY (POSIX): `lib/POSIX.pm` is a 45-name stub -- `use POSIX;` exports NOTHING (perl default-exports 587 names), so `use POSIX; floor(3.7)` DIES "Undefined subroutine &main::floor"; `use POSIX qw(strftime)` DIES at the import ("strftime" is not exported), and so do EXIT_FAILURE, mktime, setlocale/LC_ALL, the :sys_wait_h W* macros, _exit, setsid, isatty, strerror, DBL_EPSILON ... -- widens #1613 (strftime alone), which is FOLDED into this task
